study.title: Deblurring-aware semantic segmentation of crops and weeds in UAV sorghum imagery via a UNet-ResNet architecture

segmentation.domain: 3-class crop-weed semantic segmentation (background, crop/sorghum, weed) of UAV sorghum-field imagery with a UNet-ResNet encoder-decoder; systematic comparison of four ResNet encoders (18/34/50/101); explicit NAFNet deblurring front-end integrated through a restoration-aware (two-stage) training protocol to handle motion blur prevalent in UAV acquisition; joint loss Ltotal = Lseg (cross-entropy) + 0.1*Ldeblur (PSNR-oriented L1)
segmentation.best_model: UNet-ResNet34: highest mean Dice on sharp hold-out test 0.9198 (BG 0.9975 / Crop 0.9047 / Weed 0.8570), marginally ahead of ResNet-18 (0.9167), ResNet-50 (0.9154) and ResNet-101 (0.9141) - accuracy saturates with depth. With NAFNet restoration front-end: best combined-set mDS 0.8223, mIoU 0.7185 (+27.7% relative on motion-blurred subset over no-restoration baseline)

dataset.name: Public DeBlurWeedSeg dataset (Genze et al., 2023, Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/k4gvsjv4t3.1): 1,300 paired 128x128 image patches (motion-blurred + sharp counterpart) from an experimental sorghum field in Southern Germany, DJI Mavic 2 Pro consumer drone, sorghum at BBCH 13 growth stage, dominant weed Chenopodium album with minor Cirsium arvense. Three classes: background, crop (sorghum), weed. Extreme class imbalance: background 97.33%, crop 1.45% (67.31x), weed 1.23% (79.21x) of pixels. Stratified 70/15/15 train/val/test patch-level split, fixed seed 0.
dataset.note: uav_collected=false: public DeBlurWeedSeg dataset, not collected by these authors. images = 1,300 paired sharp/blurred 128x128 patches (910 train / 195 val / 195 test). GSD and flight altitude not reported in this paper. Single field/species/phenological stage; authors refrain from crop-agnostic generality claims. Augmentation: random H/V flips, 90 deg rotations, brightness/contrast jitter within 20%.

segmentation.backbone: UNet encoder-decoder with ResNet encoder backbones (Basic Block ResNet-18/34, Bottleneck ResNet-50/101), ImageNet-pretrained (torchvision) but fine-tuned trainable; 5-decoder-block decoder with nearest-neighbor 2x upsampling + skip connections, dual 3x3 Conv-BN-ReLU per block, partial projection shortcuts; segmentation head = dropout 0.1 + 3x3 conv, Kaiming/Xavier init. Training: Adam (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999), LR 1e-3 cosine to 1e-6, weight decay 1e-4, 100 epochs, batch 16. NAFNet pre-trained 150 epochs LR 1e-3 on L1; joint fine-tune LR 1e-5 for restoration params, lambda 0.1.

mIoU.quote: the proposed UNet-ResNet34 with the restoration-aware NAFNet front-end attains the highest mDS (0.8223), mIoU (0.7185) and mPrecision (0.8424) on the combined test set
mIoU.ambiguity: mIoU on the combined (sharp + motion-blurred) hold-out test set for the proposed UNet-ResNet34 + NAFNet. Baselines on combined set: U-Net++ (w/o NAF) 0.6705, FPN 0.6689, DeepLabV3+ 0.6587; all baselines DEGRADE when NAFNet is naively prepended (0.5057-0.5445) because they were trained on sharp images. Per-class IoU per encoder not tabulated; per-class Dice provided instead.

mPA.ambiguity: Mean pixel accuracy not reported; metrics are mDS, mIoU, mPrecision, mRecall.

F1.ambiguity: F1 not reported; per-class and mean Precision + Recall reported instead (mPrecision 0.8424, mRecall 0.8067 for proposed on combined test).

Dice.quote: a systematic comparison across four ResNet encoder variants (ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101) reveals that ResNet-34 achieves the highest mean Dice Score of 0.9198
Dice.ambiguity: mDS = mean Dice (eq. 19-20) over 3 classes on SHARP hold-out test, UNet-ResNet34 trained on sharp patches only. Per-class: BG 0.9975, Crop 0.9047, Weed 0.8570. Ablation: full model 0.9198; w/o skip connections 0.8847; 3 decoder blocks 0.8680; single-conv decoder 0.9160; w/o ImageNet 0.9193; w/o dropout 0.9213. With deblur front-end on combined set: 0.8223 (sharp 0.8924 / motion-blurred 0.7614).

PA.ambiguity: Pixel accuracy not reported; background class dominates 97.33% of pixels.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 not reported; per-class Weed Dice for ResNet-34 0.8570 (best, vs 0.8527 R18, 0.8492 R50, 0.8460 R101).

crop_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 not reported; per-class Crop (sorghum) Dice for ResNet-34 0.9047 (best).

edge.device: None - no on-device deployment performed. Complexity analysis targets a conceptual NVIDIA Jetson on-board pipeline (Fig. 8); 'a direct on-device throughput validation on embedded NVIDIA Jetson hardware was not performed and is left for future work'; training on a desktop NVIDIA RTX 3090 24GB
edge.framework: PyTorch 2.1.0 + segmentation-models-pytorch library; torchvision ImageNet-pretrained encoders; thop library for params/MACs; Adam optimizer, cosine annealing, mixed precision not mentioned (FP32 only)

fps.ambiguity: No throughput reported; on-device frame rates explicitly deferred to planned hardware validation.

params_M.quote: the segmentation network alone (24.4 M parameters, 1.97 GMACs) is comparable in complexity to the standard CNN baselines
params_M.ambiguity: STRUCTURAL complexity at 128x128 input (thop), segmentation-only UNet-R34 (ARCHITECTURE-level, NOT deployed/measured; edge.reported=false). NAFNet deblur adds 17.0 M (full pipeline 41.4 M). Baselines: DeepLabV3+ 22.4 M, FPN 23.2 M, U-Net++ 26.1 M.

gflops.quote: the segmentation network alone (24.4 M parameters, 1.97 GMACs) is comparable in complexity to the standard CNN baselines
gflops.ambiguity: Derived from reported 1.97 GMACs (2 FLOPs per MAC) at 128x128 input; structural/architecture-level only, NOT measured on device (edge.reported=false). NAFNet front-end adds 2.98 GMACs (5.96 GFLOPs-equiv); full pipeline 4.95 GMACs (9.90 GFLOPs-equiv). Baselines: DeepLabV3+ 1.98, FPN 1.72, U-Net++ 4.62 GMACs.

issues: edge.reported=false: only a conceptual NAFNet-deblurring + UNet-ResNet34 on-board deployment schematic (Fig. 8) and thop-based params/MACs analysis; no on-device Jetson throughput or latency measurement (explicitly future work). params_M/gflops recorded as reported architecture-level structural figures, flagged accordingly.

Primary accuracy headline is Dice (mDS 0.9198 sharp-test ResNet-34; combined deblur 0.8223); mIoU only reported for the combined-set SOTA comparison (Table 6) - recorded here as reported with that context.

uav_collected=false: uses public DeBlurWeedSeg dataset (1,300 paired sharp/blurred patches); single sorghum field, BBCH 13, C. album dominated - authors explicitly refrain from general cross-crop claims.
Single-seed (seed 0) deterministic protocol: small inter-configuration mDS gaps (~0.1-0.5 pp) treated by authors as run-to-run noise, not definitive rankings.

Dataset class imbalance extreme (background 97.33%; crop 1.45%, weed 1.23%); no explicit class-balanced/focal loss used, imbalance mitigated only implicitly via mean-class metrics, pretraining and dropout.
